pamphlet_excerpts: Immediate Blister Drainage: Once a blister forms, it is best to immediately drain (p. 18).
Fast Pain Relief: Draining the blister usually provides immediate pain relief (p. 18).
Cleaning and Ointment Application: Wash the area with soap and water and then apply a thin layer of an antibiotic ointment to prevent infection (p. 18).
Waterproof Dressing Protection: Cover with a dry dressing and hold it in place with waterproof tape or a compressive elastic bandage (p. 18).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Clean and Apply Ointment: Wash the area with soap and water and then apply a thin layer of an antibiotic ointment to prevent infection (p. 18).
Step 2 - Secure With Waterproof Tape: Cover with a dry dressing and hold it in place with waterproof tape or a compressive elastic bandage (p. 18).
Step 3 - Prevent Further Friction: This should protect the blister and prevent further friction to the affected area (p. 18).
Step 4 - Assess Cold Water Dangers: There are two primary dangers from falling into cold water (p. 18).

C. Unbuckle and remove your PFD lifejacket so you can swim faster.
D. Dive underneath the overturned cockpit to untie the stern painter line with your feet inside the hull.

pamphlet_excerpts: Paddle Grip and Comfort: In selecting a kayak paddle, the most important thing to consider is the comfort of the paddle in your hands (p. 29).
Oval Shaft Indexing Control: Quality paddles have an oval shaft, which provides better control and comfort and helps you set the correct angle (p. 29).
Straight Versus Bent Shafts: Most paddles have straight shafts, but a few designs are bent at the grip positions to ease strain on the wrists (p. 29).
Standard Centimeter Paddle Lengths: Paddles for recreational kayaks are normally sized in centimeters, with typical lengths between 200 and 220 centimeters (p. 29).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Compare Shaft Grip Designs: Most paddles have straight shafts, but a few designs are bent at the grip positions to ease strain on the wrists (p. 29).
Step 2 - Select Appropriate Centimeter Length: Paddles for recreational kayaks are normally sized in centimeters, with typical lengths between 200 and 220 centimeters (p. 29).
Step 3 - Hold Paddle Overhead Horizontally: Given these differences, a general rule of thumb for sizing akayak paddle is to hold the paddle above your head horizontally (p. 29).
Step 4 - Check Ninety-Degree Elbow Spacing: With your elbows at 90-degree angles, your hands should be 6 to 8 inches from the throat on either end of the paddle (p. 29).

pamphlet_excerpts: Low-Maintenance Kayaking Equipment: One nice thing about kayaking is that the equipment you use will be relatively maintenance free (p. 33).
Manufacturer Care Guidelines: Follow the manufacturer's instructions for specifics on the care and maintenance (p. 33).
Season-to-Season Equipment Readiness: Following these tips will help you be better prepared from season to season (p. 33).
Knuckle and Blade Alignment: When you hold a paddle, your elbows should be bent at about 90 degrees and the knuckles of your right hand should line up with the edge of your right (p. 33).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Inspect Gear Each Season: Following these tips will help you be better prepared from season to season (p. 33).

Intentional Blade Placement: When the paddle blade is put in the water, it should be placed in a way so the boat moves in the direction you want (p. 67).
Efficient Energy Transfer: Ideally, all the energy applied to the paddle should make the boat go where the paddler wants (p. 67).
Anchoring Body Contact Points: For this to happen, it helps to anchor a few things in place (p. 67).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Channel Energy Into Hull: Ideally, all the energy applied to the paddle should make the boat go where the paddler wants (p. 67).
Step 2 - Set Lower Body Anchors: For this to happen, it helps to anchor a few things in place (p. 67).
Step 3 - Brace Inside the Cockpit: First, the paddler needs to anchor himself in the boat (p. 67).
Step 4 - Drive With Lower Body: Good outfitting helps, as does gently pushing with the feet, legs, and buttocks during each paddle stroke (p. 67).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Your kayak capsizes in calm lake water during a practice paddle. After performing a wet exit, what is your immediate priority in the water?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Your kayak capsizes in calm lake water during a practice paddle. After performing a wet exit, what is your immediate priority in the water?
options: A. Abandon the kayak and paddle and try to swim 300 yards to the nearest shoreline.
B. Maintain physical contact with your capsized kayak and paddle, signal your buddy boat, and position yourself at the bow/stern for a T-rescue or heel-hook re-entry.
C. Unbuckle and remove your PFD lifejacket so you can swim faster.
D. Dive underneath the overturned cockpit to untie the stern painter line with your feet inside the hull.
choices: A. Abandon the kayak and paddle and try to swim 300 yards to the nearest shoreline.
B. Maintain physical contact with your capsized kayak and paddle, signal your buddy boat, and position yourself at the bow/stern for a T-rescue or heel-hook re-entry.
C. Unbuckle and remove your PFD lifejacket so you can swim faster.
D. Dive underneath the overturned cockpit to untie the stern painter line with your feet inside the hull.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Maintain physical contact with your capsized kayak and paddle, signal your buddy boat, and position yourself at the bow/stern for a T-rescue or heel-hook re-entry.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): A swamped kayak provides massive flotation and high visibility for rescuers, whereas swimming away in open water risks cold-water exhaustion and separation.

choices: A. Directly between the two kayaks to push the cockpit rim upward

patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): To avoid injury between colliding hulls, the swimmer moves to the far end of the capsized kayak and pushes down while the rescuer pulls it across the deck (p. 56).
